title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
abstract: arXiv:2610.22471v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: GPT-6-Astra demonstrates a level of competence in robotic manipulation and navigation that challenges the conventional paradigm of building specialized models for individual tasks and embodiments. In this report, we ask not only how capable GPT-6-Astra is, but what its capabilities imply for the field. First, we probe the limits of standalone GPT-6-Astra. We conduct a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands. Under a unified protocol that allows in-context learning (ICL) from training-set demonstrations and substantially increases the number of execution steps, GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance (Fig. 1). Future research may focus on improving 1) the generality of ICL 2) cost and execution time, 3) physical-state verification, 4) recovery from irreversible failures, and 5) long-horizon preservation of progress. translated_title: GPT-6-Astra 实现具身智能了吗？
translated_abstract: GPT-6-Astra 在机器人操作与导航方面展现出的能力水平，对为单个任务和单个机器人本体构建专用模型的传统范式提出了挑战。在本报告中，我们不仅探究 GPT-6-Astra 的能力究竟有多强，还探讨其能力对该领域意味着什么。首先，我们探究了独立运行的 GPT-6-Astra 的能力极限。我们在涵盖桌面操作、人形机器人、移动平台和灵巧手的 12 个代表性基准上进行了大规模评估。在统一协议下——该协议允许从训练集演示中进行上下文学习（ICL），并大幅增加执行步骤的数量——GPT-6-Astra 取得了前所未有的性能（图 1）。未来研究可以聚焦于改进：1）ICL 的泛化能力；2）成本与执行时间；3）物理状态验证；4）从不可逆故障中恢复的能力；以及 5）长时程任务中已获进展的保持。其次，我们研究……
tldr: 本报告通过在涵盖桌面操作、人形机器人、移动平台和灵巧手的 12 个代表性基准上进行大规模统一评估，证明 GPT-6-Astra 在机器人操作与导航任务中取得了前所未有的性能，其能力挑战了为单个任务和本体构建专用模型的传统范式，并提出了 ICL 泛化性、成本、物理状态验证、故障恢复和长时程进度保持五大未来研究方向。
en_tdlr: This report presents a large-scale evaluation across 12 representative benchmarks—spanning tabletop manipulation, humanoids, mobile platforms, and dexterous hands—showing that GPT-6-Astra achieves unprecedented performance in robotic manipulation and navigation under a unified protocol with in-context learning, challenging the conventional paradigm of building specialized models per task and embodiment, and outlining five key directions for future research.
